title: dynamic batching: seqlen bucketing and padding minimization heuristics (v16)
author: Ethan Zhao
release_notes: Improve dynamic batching heuristics: introduce seqlen bucketing with cost-aware padding minimization; scheduler updates to prefer low-padding batches and reduce KV-cache thrashing. Expected throughput +8-12% for mixed-seqlen workloads; no API changes.
description: Motivation: mixed sequence length workloads (chat + few-shot prompts) cause high padding overhead in continuous batching. This PR introduces an updated dynamic-batching heuristic (v16) that creates seqlen buckets using an adaptive histogram, assigns incoming requests to buckets to minimize padding, and updates the scheduler to avoid KV-cache thrashing by preferring batches that preserve cache locality. Changes are backward-compatible from an API perspective. What I changed: - new seqlen bucketing module: runtime/scheduler/seqlen_bucketing.{cc,h} - padding minimizer: runtime/scheduler/padding_minimizer.{cc,h} - scheduler policy: runtime/scheduler/policy_v2.cc (prefers same-model, same-kv-shard batches when possible) - updated kernel invocation path to emit smaller contiguous token ranges for mixed-length batches (runtime/kernel/launch.cc) - perf harness updates and new unit + integration tests (tests/scheduler/*) - added canary rollout config (deploy/rollout/dynamic-batching-canary.yaml) Checklist: [x] Benchmark results show throughput and cost improvements for mixed workloads (see perf_results) [x] Unit tests added and passing (tests/scheduler) [x] Integration tests including KV-cache warmup scenarios added [x] Feature-gated behind `enable_seqlen_bucketing` runtime flag (default true for canary clusters) Implementation notes: - Bucketing: we maintain an online histogram of observed sequence lengths per model and recompute bucket boundaries every 30s using a lightweight greedy partitioner to cap intra-bucket padding at a target percentile (configurable). - Padding minimization: when assembling a batch we evaluate candidate buckets and prefer the bucket that reduces aggregate padding cost while respecting latency SLOs. We model padding cost as weighted tokens padded * kernel_cost_per_token to account for non-linear kernel overheads on long sequences. - KV-cache locality: scheduler prefers grouping requests that map to the same KV shard and similar past KV cache state to avoid repeated cache evictions. When necessary, it will trade small padding increases for cache locality if the predicted token execution cost predicts net win. - Kernel path changes: adjusted the continuous batching path to produce per-bucket tensor packing and annotated kernel launches so GPU kernels can use smaller memory footprints and reduce memcpy overhead for padded tails. Testing and rollout: - Unit and integration tests added: tests/scheduler/test_bucketing.py, tests/scheduler/test_padding_minimizer.py, tests/scheduler/test_kv_locality_integration.py - Perf harness: added workload profiles for chat-heavy mixed-length traces and synthetic mixed histograms. - Canary rollout: apply to 5% of serving fleet for 48h, monitor token throughput, 99th latency, and KV-cache miss rate. Related Linear/Jira: ENG-4521 (dynamic batching revamp), PERF-217 (mixed-seqlen perf), ENG-4875 (kv-cache locality optimizations). Notes for reviewers: the core algorithm is in seqlen_bucketing.{cc,h} and padding_minimizer.{cc,h}. The scheduler changes are intentionally conservative: we only change batch selection heuristics and leave preemption and SLO enforcement untouched. Performance profiles attached below.

review_comments: Aisha Patel: Overall approach looks good. Two questions: 1) how do we avoid pathological bucket oscillation on highly bimodal workloads? 2) please add a graceful fallback when histogram stats are sparse.

Ethan Zhao: Answered: we use an inertia term and min-observation threshold before recomputing boundaries; added unit test for sparse histograms (see test_bucketing). Also added a max-change-per-interval guard to avoid oscillation.
Miguel Santos: Can you run the canary on a dedicated KV-shard stress profile? I saw a small regression in 99th for one profile in earlier runs.

Ethan Zhao: Ran targeted canary with KV-shard stress profile, fixed a hot path in policy_v2 where locality preference over-selected large-batches causing temporary memory pressure. Updated selection logic and re-ran benchmarks. Results in perf_results below.
Priya Raman: Please add telemetry for "bucket_assignment" and "padding_saved_tokens" metrics. Also suggest making the bucket recompute interval configurable via runtime flags.
Ethan Zhao: Added metrics and made recompute interval configurable (runtime flag). Updated docs/notes and telemetry mapping.
Aisha Patel: Approving after perf numbers look stable on canary.
Miguel Santos: Approved - no concerns remain.
